comparisons.peer_topic: QCT segment revenue drivers and EBT margin change
comparisons.peer_summary: QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 increased primarily due to higher handset revenues driven by $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments from major OEMs and higher automotive revenues from new vehicle launches with Snapdragon products, partially offset by lower IoT revenues; QCT EBT as a percentage of revenues increased primarily due to these higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA discloses strategic partnerships and platform adoption to drive its automotive segment (MediaTek, Foxconn, BYD, etc.). QCOM discloses that its automotive revenue growth was primarily driven by demand from new vehicle launches utilizing its Snapdragon digital cockpit and connectivity products. Both disclosures illustrate a reliance on OEM relationships and vehicle launch cycles to drive automotive segment performance, though NVDA focuses on collaborative platform development while QCOM focuses on component adoption in new vehicles.
